Vera UI redesign - v26

- Canvas to context edges follow the same rule as chat to canvas: only coloured when the item belongs to the turn in focus. Everything else is a quiet hairline, and the node it lands on dims with it.
- Full / Hover / Zen now apply to the composer too: Hover reveals the chip r

CHAT — the one chat UI is the tri-page in its chat-only state, embedded here at 1440×1000. Everything on it is the tri-page board's own code: the header (detail, Blocks, Explode with Cards · Front · Iso, + Canvas / + Graph, the context meter, the mode, the tools, Aa), the LHM rail whose entries are

CHAT SIDE MENU — where all 13 tabs went (the 5 groups), then the ONE chat UI live with its quick menu open: click the rail for each menu; Context expands into the full graph. The chat is the tri-page board embedded — nothing here is a second implementation.

GRAPH — the one chat UI with the context graph open (the tri-page embedded with chat + graph). The Context menu expands into the full graph beside the rail; the records in the focused turn's context run to the message that read them; click a message or a loop step to refocus; drag / wheel / Fit on t

LIVE OPERATIONS — edges are pipes: they run along the lanes of their own plane, then straight up or down to the next, and they are colour-coded by kind with a key beside the map. A node's box on the graph IS the action surface — Metrics, Terminal, Files, Send request, Capabilities, Logs — in 2D and

HARNESS — Agentic activity is a row IN the layout, not an overlay: opening it shortens the dashboard instead of covering it, in both tab and side-menu modes. It lists every running and recent loop, dream, goal, program and run, and each opens its own detail modal. Switch to the side menu (☰) and liv
SETTINGS — the 34 deep sections: 14 Config, 14 Loop, 6 Context.
FEATURE AUDIT — all 163 CH.* handlers swept from source, grouped into 15 areas with a destination each.
STYLE PACKS — four packs on the same nine components, and the variables each declares.

WIDGET GALLERY - sixty-five still forms at six columns, each frame wider than before. A widget is a FORM plus a CONFIG: the form is the drawing code, the config says what it reads, how big it is, which palette, whether it animates, whether it carries a legend. Nothing here is welded to one measure.

TRI-PAGE — chat · canvas · graph, the one chat UI, 2560×1280. The chat column is the real chat (rail 46 + chat 414 = the old 460, so the canvas and the graph sit exactly where they did); the edges leave from the message they belong to — the transcript is measured after every render — and land on the

WIDGETS - MOTION, COMPOSITES, CONFIG - twenty-seven widgets that move, plus what they are built on. Eight new dynamic forms, none of them a bar chart: an orbit of running agents, a tank with a wave and a feed pipe, a turbine at the token rate, an oscilloscope trace with a sweep head, pulse rings per

WIDGET CONFIG - the editor for the record every widget is made from. Left: the catalogue, fifty-five forms grouped by the SHAPE they read, each marked flat/iso, still/moves, and whether it has a live build here. Middle: the record - identity, source (only sources of the right shape are offered, with

PRE-IMPLEMENTATION QC - every board rendered in the real preview runtime and checked by the lint, shape, binding and smoke passes and the numeric edge checker, then read by eye. Left: board by board - what is verified, what was fixed this round, what is open, what blocks. Right: the six contracts th

GLOBE WIDGETS - godseye on the canvas. One globe form, six configs: events of the last hour, the estate with its links, market sessions on the day side, weather at the three places the machines are, alerts as flags on posts over a globe on a plinth, and the same globe at rail size. The discipline is

PANELS DRIVEN BY THE LLM - a turn can carry directives: open this panel, set that one, pin this, focus the rail. Each lands as a chip on the message, a ribbon on the panel it drove and a row in the log; the policy per panel is yours - let it drive, ask first, never - and undo is one click. Policy ch

HOW THE LLM DRIVES THE UI — one vocabulary of directives (panels, canvas, LHM, widgets, chat, graph, scripts), one dispatcher (policy · apply · log · ribbon · event), two paths: DIRECT (the model issues a directive in its tool loop or inline in a reply) and SCRIPTED (deterministic on · if · do rules

SIZES - XS TO XL. A size is a composition, not a scale: XS sits in a line of text (glyph + one figure), S is a chip or a row on a graph node, M is the gallery cell, L adds the detail list beside it, XL adds the table, the log and the actions. A composite is a report - real detail line for line, with

FORMATS, STREAMING, WIDGETS IN THE REPLY. Left: everything a reply may contain, rendered - headings, tables with a sort, a diff-marked code block with copy/open/apply, task lists, callouts, quotes, a formula, attachments, figures, footnotes. Top right: a mermaid block rendered AS THE TOKENS ARRIVE -

DASHBOARD IN EDIT MODE. Every tile is a widget record from the gallery, dropped on a 6-column grid of 112px rows. Nothing the old dashboard did is lost: edit mode, drag to move (Live events is mid-drag, the ghost shows where it lands), drag a corner to resize (the readout says the span), snap to the

THE WIDGET SYSTEM, READY TO IMPLEMENT. The record schema with every field and its rule; the composite record (slots, children by value or by id, $subject binding, the report template); the shape, source and form registries; the size ladder and the span-to-size rule; the dashboard layout record; plac

ONE SYSTEM. The seam between panels driven by the LLM, the chat canvas and the widget system, drawn once. Two lanes: a TURN goes through the context surfacer (facts to the model, affordances and representations to the canvas as suggestions), the model replies with prose, widget fences and directives

THE UNIFIED GRAPH, FOUR WAYS. One session, one dataset: turns, context (eight sources), memory (injected and related), a DAG-flow run (parallel checks, a retry, a gate, a sub-DAG, a skipped branch), an agentic v7 loop (assess · plan · execute · review in cycles, a git-tree branch chosen by review, a

PASTED INTO THE CHAT — the one chat UI live with attachments (the tri-page embedded, paste=yes): six chips with the size guard, the active chip's inline editor, a drop band, a question carrying two attachments; press Attach to toggle. Then the spec: what a paste or drop becomes, and what the model s

WIDGETS · ISOMETRIC, THIRD PAGE. Twenty-four more iso forms, every one a record: twelve shaped like the parts of a SharePoint site (document library, pages, list, calendar, people, news, tasks, files, approvals, wiki, form, notices) and twelve from Vera's suites (markets, business ops, mesh, noteboo

ARRIVALS. How things come into the UI, looping: a chat turn lands and is stamped; a graph node pops and its edge draws; a canvas item rises into the NOW band while the items below make room; a widget mounts its frame, shows a skeleton, then its content and bars; a dashboard tile drops with a settle

Widget adoption: where widgets can live (the host matrix), which existing UI elements become widgets to stop reproduction (the adoption list, with file and panel names from the repo), and the rule for when an element must be a widget. Pretty much everything should be a widget.

WIDGET REGISTRY — every configuration of a widget used anywhere (dashboard, canvas, a menu, a reply, a notebook, the ops map, an iso plate) can be saved as a template with ⧉ and placed again anywhere from any picker. One record: form + config; the envelope is the surface's. The capability contract w
